blocks.heading: Separating the trailer from the game
blocks.body:
Fox Stories presented a cozy adventure, but the implemented prototype was much smaller. Players could explore and pick up items; the trailer’s NPC interactions were scripted. Stealing, progression, and a sustained gameplay loop were not implemented.

The response to the trailer outpaced the game. It pushed us to ask what the player actually does and how that role connects them to the world.

blocks.heading: The fantasy traveled further than the prototype
blocks.body: The response was exciting, but it exposed the gap between a world people wanted and a game we knew how to make. I keep the number here as evidence of resonance, not as proof that the design was solved.
